text.4: How This Book Works This is not an ordinary word search. Every puzzle hides a sentence. 1. Find and cross out every word in the list. They run in all eight directions, including backwards. 2. Read the letters you did not cross out, left to right and top to bottom. They spell a statement of fact about the night Sir Ambrose Pell died. 3. Four puzzles make one chapter, and one chapter clears one suspect. Cross that name off the list at the front of the book. 4. When eleven names are gone, the twelfth is your answer — and the final chapter will confirm it. A promise. Every clue in this book is true, every alibi holds, and exactly one person can be guilty. The solution has been checked by machine: no chapter is redundant, and no second suspect survives all twelve. Solutions to every grid begin on the page marked Answers. Try not to look. 4
text.5: The Case THISTLEWICK HALL · JANUARY 1927 Sir Ambrose Pell held Thistlewick Hall for forty years, and kept its secrets longer. On the night of the eleventh of January he was found in the orangery, beneath the citrus trees his father had planted. The door was bolted on the inside. The key was not in the room, nor anywhere else in the house. It froze hard that night, and no print was left on the terrace. Twelve people at the Hall had reason to wish Sir Ambrose gone. Eleven of them can prove where they were. Your task is to find out which eleven. Cross off each name as you clear it. 5
text.6: The Twelve Abel Stoke Butler. Pell promised him the lodge, then let it to another man. Martha Grigg Cook. Thirty years at that range and no pension ever written down. Josiah Rudd Gamekeeper. Pell threatened him with dismissal over the poaching. Will Catchpole Groom. Pell sold the hunter he had raised from a foal. Esther Vane Lady's maid. Pell accused her of taking a brooch she never touched. Ned Harrow Gardener. Came from Thistlewick Green, where he was turned out once before. Hannah Dunnock Housekeeper. Pell refused to let her widowed sister have the lodge. Albert Crane Chauffeur. Pell blamed him for the broken engine and docked his wages. Horace Finch Solicitor. Pell was about to take the estate's business elsewhere. Samuel Ash Estate carpenter. Pell had not paid him for the chapel timber. Clara Wynne Governess.
